cohort: 50 pregnant teenagers (13-19 years old) compared to 50 pregnant women (20-29 years old) without medical or surgical disorders excluding anemia and protein energy malnutrition.
finding: Teenage mothers had a significantly higher occurrence of mild anemia, severe pre-eclampsia, preterm labor, UTI, induction of labor, low birth weight, birth asphyxia, and NICU admission compared to older mothers.
birth_weight: Low birth weight mentioned as an outcome, but no specific ranges given
